correctness.rationale: Two independent face tests agree on all 65,536 subsets; each of two complete pivot-order Morse matchings has 16,191 pairs and precisely one critical vertex and seven critical seven-cells. Complete Kahn acyclicity checks on 218,672 Hasse incidences and 32,390 faces per matching certify Forman acyclicity. Therefore the CW model is a wedge of seven 7-spheres. Signed Lefschetz enumeration across all eight graph rotations yields the rational character; bipartition and a perfect matching establish vertex-cover number eight.

value.rationale: The Möbius–Kantor graph is a canonical symmetric cubic eight-point incidence graph, not an ad hoc slice. Its exact dominance homotopy and C8 character exhibit a seven-generator and nontrivial symmetry phenomenon at sharp equality in the general vertex-cover/connectivity theorem; neither the inequality nor familiar independence/matching types determine the result. The precise graph and character are natural benchmarks for nonchordal dominance complexes, without asserting an arbitrary family-wide theorem.
